title: Tea, iced, instant, black, pre-sweetened, dry

content.title: About
content.content: Iced instant black tea, pre‑sweetened, is a convenient beverage that prepares quickly by adding hot or cold water. The dry powder retains the black tea aroma and sweetness, allowing you to enjoy a refreshing drink without extra sweetening.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black tea is the most widely consumed type of tea worldwide, with production dating back over 2,000 years in China.
Instant tea was invented in the early 20th century for the convenience of soldiers and travelers.
Pre‑sweetening is usually done with sugar or glucose syrup, making the drink ready to consume immediately after reconstitution.
Dry instant teas are commonly used in commercial vending machines and office kitchens.
Black tea contains caffeine, which can boost alertness and concentration.

items.title: Energizing effect
items.content: Black tea contains caffeine, which may improve focus and increase energy levels.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Tea provides polyphenols such as theaflavins and thearubigins that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Moderate regular consumption of black tea may support vascular function and lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Warm tea can help relax the stomach and ease digestion.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Despite its caffeine content, tea contributes to daily fluid intake when consumed in moderate amounts.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: People sensitive to caffeine may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Pre‑sweetened tea contains added sugars, which can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries with frequent use.

items.title: Tea allergy
items.content: Rarely, individuals may have an allergic reaction to tea components.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Caffeine can amplify the effects of certain stimulants and reduce the efficacy of some sedative drugs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add 1‑2 teaspoons of the dry powder to 200‑250 ml of hot or cold water, stir until fully dissolved. For a cooler drink, add ice, a slice of lemon, or mint for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the tea packet in a dry, cool place, tightly sealed. Keep moisture out to prevent clumping and flavor loss.
